newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan new crop cotton rate rises on shortage.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan new crop cotton rate rises on shortage.

text.p: Pakistan's new crop NIAB-78 cotton variety closed 28 rupees higher at 2,673 on Sunday, the official start of the new crop season, dealers said.
They said the rate was likely to rise further on Monday.
NIAB-78 traded at 2,425 in the kerb amid higher demand from spinners and low supplies from farms, broker Nasim Usman said.
The private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) stopped quoting prices for old crop K-68 and MNH-93 varieties.

The KCA said exports had reached 1.82 million 375-lb bales by August 25 in the 1995/96 crop season. Dealers had registered 2.33 million bales for export with the state-run Export Promotion Bureau by June 3, the KCA said.
